scope: Missing CWP-related activists and the Stony Brook custody roster; adds absent identities only.

sbu_roster.label: Statesman, March 21, 1969, printed p.1/PDF p.1. Named 21-person library-protest roster and separate Michael Zweig contempt report; visually reviewed.

sbu_custody.label: Statesman, March 27, 1969, printed p.1/PDF p.1, 21 Students To Be Freed on Friday. Jail officials describe ongoing custody and conditional prospective release; visually reviewed.

sbu_feb1970.label: Statesman, February 23, 1970, printed p.4/PDF p.1, Justice at Hauppauge. Cohen and Kissack actual weekend custody and respective sentences; visually reviewed.

sbu_nov1970.label: Statesman, November 10, 1970, printed p.1/PDF p.1, Wechsler Given 14 Months. October 26 remand and November 9 sentence; visually reviewed.

cwp_calderon.label: Workers Viewpoint, September 30-October 13, 1981, p.7, Jose Calderon Jailed While Murderers Remain Free. Actual September 21 prison entry; visually reviewed. Party allegations about other actors are not adopted as fact.

nga.label: National Governors Association, 1980 Annual Meeting proceedings, p.63. Eyewitness transcript and editorial disposition note: assault conviction and January 1981 thirty-day sentence.

tung_author.label: Jerry Tung, The Socialist Road, About the Author. Links the Stony Brook organizer to subsequent CWP leadership. Promotional claims not adopted as independent findings.

ira_obit.label: Progressive Labor Party, January 2, 2025 obituary of Ira Wechsler. Stony Brook SDS and PLP affiliation; vital dates held pending explicit year confirmation.

prisoner.name: Mitch Cohen
prisoner.description: Mitch Cohen was a Stony Brook campus activist jailed after his arrest while challenging exclusion from campus. His case helped prompt the March 1969 library protest.

cases.charges: Criminal trespass and resisting arrest
cases.sentence: Concurrent terms of four months and three months. Confirmed in county jail over the February 1970 weekend; subsequent release and actual total remain unverified.

entries.custody_evidence: The February 23 editorial explicitly reports Cohen and Kissack spent the weekend in county jail after sentencing.

prisoner.name: Glenn Kissack
prisoner.description: Glenn Kissack was a Stony Brook student jailed after intervening in the arrest of campus activist Mitch Cohen.

cases.charges: Harassment and obstructing governmental administration
cases.sentence: Ten days and a $100 fine. Confirmed in county jail over the February 1970 weekend; full service and release date remain unverified.

entries.custody_evidence: The February 23 editorial explicitly reports Kissack and Cohen spent the weekend in county jail after sentencing.

prisoner.name: Michael Zweig
prisoner.description: Michael Zweig, a Stony Brook economics professor, was jailed for refusing to answer grand-jury questions about students during a campus drug investigation. Faculty and students organized support for his refusal.

cases.charges: Criminal contempt — refusal to answer grand-jury questions
cases.sentence: Ten days and a $200 fine. The March 21, 1969 newspaper reports he remained jailed following the Tuesday sentence. Actual release and total time served remain unverified.

entries.custody_evidence: The March 21 article reports Tuesday sentencing and says Zweig is being held; it also describes Wednesday faculty support for the incarcerated professor.

prisoner.name: Jose Calderon
prisoner.description: Jose Calderon was a Northern Colorado community activist and Communist Workers Party spokesperson jailed after an egg-throwing protest during John Anderson’s speech at the 1980 governors meeting. His protest concerned the Greensboro killings.

cases.charges: Assault on a congressman
cases.sentence: Thirty-day jail sentence imposed in January 1981. Began serving September 21, 1981. Exact release and completed duration remain unverified.

entries.custody_evidence: The September 30-October 13 party newspaper reports Calderon began serving September 21 and describes him as jailed; the governors proceedings independently confirm the protest, conviction and sentence.
